description: Language reference, standard libraries, asynchronous concurrency, and data structures.
text: Python is a high-level, dynamically typed language emphasizing readability and developer productivity. Key data structures include lists (ordered, mutable), tuples (ordered, immutable), sets (unordered, unique), and dictionaries (hash tables with O(1) average lookup). Python 3.5+ supports asynchronous programming via asyncio, using async/await syntax to manage non-blocking I/O operations cooperatively on an event loop.

description: Android app architecture, activities, services, background location, and hardware sensor listeners.
text: Android applications are built with four primary components: Activities (UI windows), Services (background tasks), Broadcast Receivers (system event listeners), and Content Providers (data management). Modern Android emphasizes Jetpack architecture with ViewModels, StateFlow, and Coroutines. Access to hardware sensors requires SensorManager and SensorEventListener with runtime permissions: ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION, CAMERA, and RECORD_AUDIO. Background execution is coordinated through WorkManager.

description: Core principles of algebra, calculus, geometry, probability, and logical reasoning.
text: Mathematical reasoning involves deductive and inductive logic. Key algebraic identities: (a+b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2, and a^2 - b^2 = (a-b)(a+b). In calculus, the derivative f'(x) represents the instantaneous rate of change of a function, while the definite integral represents the accumulated net area beneath a curve. In probability, Bayes' Theorem calculates conditional probability: P(A|B) = [P(B|A) * P(A)] / P(B).

description: Newtonian mechanics, thermodynamics, electromagnetism, and cellular biology.
text: Classical physics is governed by Newton's Three Laws of Motion: 1. An object in motion remains in motion unless acted upon by an external net force (Inertia). 2. Force equals mass times acceleration (F = ma). 3. Every action has an equal and opposite reaction. The First Law of Thermodynamics dictates that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed. Cellular biology identifies DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) as the universal genetic code, transcribing information into mRNA for ribosomal protein synthesis.
